gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-vai: Wide, crisp and a little stern. Azonix leads with round-pen letters, while Noto Sans Vai follows in solid word-blocks with generous room between curve ends and stems.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-traditional-nu: Noto Traditional Nushu reads with a broad-nibbed stroke that never curls shut. Across a full page, its bowls fill the line and the text feels friendly and steady, a gentle counterweight to the stiff, swell-free Azonix above.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-numans: Azonix looks like bent paperclip wire, with no swelling anywhere. It commands the top, while Numans does the quieter work below, its s ends hanging far from the spine and its tracking pushed wide.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-oxygen: Azonix comes in wide-mouthed and commanding, its lines drawn as if by a fixed-width nib. And Oxygen follows with curves that never close on themselves and lowercase nearly matching its capitals, so a long read feels open and easy.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-pathway-extreme: Pathway Extreme reads clean and modern, with clear openings in its rounded letters and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height. And Azonix, held at fixed stylus pressure, can sit noticeably larger above it.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-readex-pro: Authoritative, this heading. Azonix is wide and commanding, and Readex Pro then reads with broad terminal gaps and a steady weight, so paragraphs below it move along without any fuss.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-sarpanch: Azonix has a round bowl whose outline never swells or thins. It is built to command attention, whereas Sarpanch is built to be read, with a clearly open lowercase e and a compact gap up to its ascenders.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-sintony: Outlines drawn in a single width, crisp and wide. Sintony then takes over with a chunky, tall midzone and smooth curves that never clog, giving Azonix a body that feels friendly beneath it.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-sofia-sans-semi-con: Azonix is commanding, with capitals barely taller than its lowercase and wide letters that stay crisp. And Sofia Sans Semi Condensed picks up below, its lowercase nearly matching capital height and each curve entered with a big visible opening.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-stack-sans-headline: Wide, stern and crisp when shrunk. Stack Sans Headline then supplies the strongest single quality of the pair: a deep middle band with a monoline skeleton and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes sharp.
